plugin.name: Translator
plugin.description: Translates as you type after “tr”, “fy” or “翻译” (“tr hello”, “tr ja good morning”, “tr en>zh apple”), with Google Translate’s web endpoint, MyMemory or DeepL. Text is sent only after one of these prefixes.
command.translate.title: Translate
command.translate.keywords: translate, translator, translation, tr, fy, deepl, google translate
pref.target.title: Translate into
pref.target.description: The language text goes into when the query names none. Automatic: the language of the interface, or English for text already in it (Simplified Chinese for English text in the English interface).
pref.engines.title: Engines
pref.engines.description: The engines asked, in order, one row each: google (Google Translate’s web endpoint: no key, not an official API, may stop working; usually unreachable in mainland China), mymemory (MyMemory by Translated: no key, about 5,000 characters a day, 50,000 with an email address), deepl (DeepL API: needs a key). Engines that need a key are skipped until it is set. The text after the prefix is sent to each of them.
pref.fallback.title: Use MyMemory when the others fail
pref.fallback.description: When every engine above fails (no connection, quota exhausted), ask MyMemory instead.
pref.selection.title: Translate selected text at once
pref.selection.description: Shows the translation of the text selected in another app in the “Selected Text” section as soon as the launcher opens. This sends the selected text to the first engine before you pick anything, so it is off by default.
pref.deeplKey.title: DeepL API key
pref.deeplKey.description: From your DeepL account (the free plan has 500,000 characters a month; its keys end in “:fx”). Stored in the Windows Credential Manager or the macOS Keychain. With a key, DeepL is asked first.
pref.mymemoryEmail.title: Email address for MyMemory
pref.mymemoryEmail.description: Optional: MyMemory allows about 50,000 characters a day instead of 5,000 with a valid email address, which is sent with each request.
